objective: Remove temp folders that an earlier Glimmervoid process left under the host scratch root (<glimmervoid home>/scratch) when it stopped mid-run. Today makeHostScratchDirectory in server/host-scratch.ts creates mkdtemp folders for Coherence readings, checks, adopt, the session feed and the factory, and each caller removes its own folder only when it finishes, so a restart or crash orphans the folder forever. Observed 2026-10-18: a service restart at 09:14:27 left coherence-regulate-1tzK9O (21 MB) behind. Fix it once, at the source: the scratch prefixes become one exported list that makeHostScratchDirectory takes its prefix from, and the server sweeps orphans of those prefixes once at startup.
criteria: A second launch refused with EADDRINUSE removes nothing.
CHANGELOG.md gains one operator-facing line under ## [Unreleased] saying leftover scratch folders are now cleaned at startup.
Every prefix passed to makeHostScratchDirectory comes from one exported list, and the prefix parameter is typed from that list, so a new caller cannot create a scratch folder the sweep does not know.
npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test pass.
Once per server start, after the dashboard port is bound, every folder directly under the scratch root whose name is a listed prefix followed by a mkdtemp suffix is removed.

One regression test drives the real sweep against a real temp scratch root: a stale listed-prefix folder is removed, while glimmervoid-hooks, an unknown name and a folder created by the same process survive.
The sweep is async; a folder that cannot be removed is logged and skipped, and startup continues.
The sweep never removes a folder this process created, never removes glimmervoid-hooks or any name that does not match a listed prefix, and never follows a symlink out of the scratch root.

authority.boundary: Live glimmervoid repository. Change only the scratch helper, its pure core, the startup call site, the one regression test and the CHANGELOG entry. No change to any caller's own cleanup, to factory code, to guardrails, or to package or tsconfig files. No new dependency.
